name: dsh-baton-mcp

tools.name: dsh_list_workspaces
tools.description: List the DeepSeek Harness workspaces (project folders): id, path, title and session_count. The id is the workspace_id for dsh_send. Read-only. Needs the dsh-baton-host plugin.

tools.name: dsh_list_sessions
tools.description: List Harness sessions, newest first, to find a session_id: session_id, title, cwd, updated_at, running, bridge_runs and model (what its next request uses). No paging: raise limit or narrow it with cwd or query. Read-only. Sessions not in dsh_list_sessions are archived or gone: do not look for them on disk.

cwd.description: Only sessions of this workspace folder

query.description: Case-insensitive text to match in title, folder or session id

tools.name: dsh_list_models
tools.description: List the models this DeepSeek Harness can run (provider, model id, name, reasoning efforts) and its default model, to check a name before passing model to dsh_send. Read-only. Needs the dsh-baton-host plugin.

tools.name: dsh_read_session
tools.description: Read the last messages of a session (role, time, text and the names of tools called; no tool output), to catch up before continuing it. Read-only.

session_id.description: Session id from dsh_list_sessions, e.g. session-…

last.description: How many of the most recent messages to return; total_messages tells how many there are

tools.name: dsh_send
tools.description: Hand a task to DeepSeek Harness, or continue a session: returns at once with a run_id and a hint saying how to wait for the reply; follow it. Call it directly, no need to list anything first. A new session starts in the folder this conversation works in, or in cwd or workspace_id (a new cwd is registered first); session_id continues that session. message arrives verbatim as a user message, and Harness does not see this conversation: make it self-contained, in the user's language, the full, explicit spec, asking for tests that cover each requirement. For a large task, write a concrete spec (goal, modules and the files each owns, level of detail, acceptance criteria) rather than passing the user's words on, and send independent parts to separate sessions in parallel, each owning its own files; review once all are back, then send specific fixes. With checks, a short request for a sub-agent review table is appended. To a busy session, mode followup queues the message and steer adds it to the running turn; left out, the Harness setting decides.

message.description: The task or reply to send

cwd.description: Workspace folder for a new session; leave out to use the folder this conversation works in

workspace_id.description: Harness workspace for a new session (from dsh_list_workspaces)

mode.description: followup queues after the current turn; steer injects into a running turn. Omit to follow Harness's busy-send setting

model.description: Only when the user names a model for this run (e.g. "DeepSeek-V4 Pro", "v4-pro"); leave out otherwise and the session uses its own model, or Harness's default model for a new session. Matched against Harness's model list ignoring case, spaces, hyphens and a leading DeepSeek; a name that matches no model or several fails the send with the list (provider/model picks one). Sets this session only; Harness's default model is left as it was

reasoning_effort.description: Only when the user names a reasoning effort, e.g. high; one of the efforts dsh_list_models shows for the model

checks.description: The project's own test commands, e.g. npm test; never check scripts you write yourself. dsh-baton runs them in the folder when the run ends and returns exit codes and the last output lines as evidence.

tools.name: dsh_status
tools.description: Look once at a run without waiting: state (queued/running/waiting/completed/failed/cancelled/interrupted), recent events, final reply, waiting_on (sub-agents or jobs still working) and human_interjections. Never a way to wait: use dsh_wait.

tools.name: dsh_wait
tools.description: Wait for a run sent with dsh_send to end and return its state and final reply. Prefer the background wait_command from dsh_send if your client wakes you when a background command exits: it costs no turns. It also returns at once when the run stops to ask a person: needs_input answer (question and relay; reply with dsh_answer) or harness-ui (an approval only a person can give in Harness). Each call waits up to 50 s; if it returns timed_out: true, call dsh_wait again with the same run_id, without a progress note.

tools.name: dsh_answer
tools.description: Answer the questions a waiting run asked (needs_input: answer in dsh_wait or dsh_status). If the user told you to decide such questions yourself, choose by your own judgment of the question and the task, call dsh_answer with reason (one sentence on why), then tell the user what you chose and why. Otherwise relay the questions to the user and start with your own advice, on a line of its own: "My recommendation: <option>, because <reason>", the reason drawn from your own judgment of the question and the task (harness_suggested only shows what the asking model would pick; it is never a reason by itself, and your pick may differ). Then list the options, wait for the user's decision and submit it with dsh_answer. Never answer on the user's behalf without that permission. Per question: option numbers or labels in choose, text for a free answer, or skip. The answer reaches Harness once every question has one (submitted: true; remaining lists the rest); then wait for the run again. If the user already answered in Harness, it reports that there is no open question.

run_id.description: Run id that is waiting (needs_input: answer)

answers.description: One entry per question answered now

id.description: Question id from question.questions[].id; may be left out when there is one question

choose.description: Option numbers (1 = first) or labels; one for a single-choice question

reason.description: Required when the user let you decide: one sentence on why you chose this, from your own judgment of the question and the task; it is returned for you to tell the user and not sent to Harness

tools.name: dsh_cancel
tools.description: Stop everything a session is doing (turn, sub-agents, background jobs, reminders), by run_id or session_id; the session is kept. Messages queued in it are dropped too (removed_from_queue); to drop one queued message use dsh_update_queued. Safe to repeat. Returns still_busy, activity and removed_from_queue.

run_id.description: Run id from dsh_send; stops the session that run belongs to

session_id.description: Session id, to stop work dsh-baton did not start

tools.name: dsh_call
tools.description: Call a dsh-baton tool by name, for a tool this conversation does not list (dsh-baton was updated without a restart; the update note names it). Runs the same code as a direct call, so it can do whatever that tool does. An unknown name changes nothing and returns the tools with their input schemas.

name.description: Tool name, e.g. dsh_send or a tool added by an update

arguments.description: Arguments for that tool, as its input schema describes them (see the list returned for an unknown name)

instructions: Hands tasks to a local DeepSeek Harness and brings the results back: start with dsh_send.
